summary: Tunisia's Foreign Ministry lists the nationalities that can enter visa-free — including every EU state except Cyprus, the UK, the US, Canada and Japan — and says the visa requirement applies to every country not on the list; its table states no length of stay. Nationalities outside the list apply for a consular visa.

passportValidity.text: The UK FCDO says your passport should be valid for the duration of your stay and in good condition: travellers who enter with a damaged or torn passport may have difficulty leaving.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tunisia entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes insurance a condition of entry for visa-exempt tourists. The UK government advises insurance for local treatment and medical evacuation: there is no free medical care for foreign nationals, and doctors' fees, medicines and private-clinic treatment must be paid on the spot.

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read requires a return or onward ticket. The UK FCDO says border officials have the right to ask for your onward or return ticket, proof of a hotel booking or other accommodation details, and your contact details, and that a small number of visitors have been refused entry or delayed for lack of evidence of accommodation.

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Tunisia. The UK Foreign Office says border officials may ask for your contact details, your onward or return travel tickets and proof of a hotel booking or other accommodation; it does not mention funds.

source.name: UK FCDO — Tunisia entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: Any import or export of foreign currency worth TND 20,000 or more must be declared to Customs on entry, on exit and in transit. A non-resident can take out more than TND 5,000 of the foreign banknotes they brought in only if they declared them on entry, and at most TND 30,000 (above that, through a bank); the declaration is valid for 3 months and one trip, and can be made online in advance. Tunisian dinars may not be taken out of the country, so keep exchange receipts to reconvert leftover dinars before you leave.

notes: The UK FCDO says Tunisia has strict currency controls: check whether you must declare foreign currency on arrival (failure to declare may lead to confiscation), and keep declaration documents and official exchange receipts.
The UK FCDO says it is illegal to bring drones into Tunisia without authorisation; any drone detected will be confiscated and stored until your departure.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to parts of western Tunisia, including the Chaambi Mountains National Park and designated military operations zones, and to areas along the Libyan border, because of cross-border terrorist activity. The Government of Canada says a state of emergency has been in effect since 2015 and is regularly extended because of the threat of terrorism.

tips.text: The Government of Canada says importing and exporting Tunisian dinars is prohibited, so exchange money in Tunisia. The UK FCDO advises keeping official exchange receipts.

If you overstay your allowance without a valid reason you will be fined; the UK Foreign Office says you can pay on departure at the airport or in advance at some police stations. The Government of Canada says to contact a Tunisian embassy or consulate before departure if you wish to stay more than 90 days.

The UK FCDO advises against all travel to the Chaambi Mountains National Park, the designated military operations zones and parts of the Algerian and Libyan border areas. The Government of Canada advises avoiding all travel to fenced-off military zones such as the area south of Remada, in Tataouine governorate.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tunisia?
faq.answer: Tunisia's Foreign Ministry table lists the nationalities that can enter visa-free, including citizens of the EU (except Cyprus), the UK, the US, Canada, Japan, Argentina, Brazil and Chile, and says the visa requirement applies to every country not on the list. Those nationalities need a consular visa before travel.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Tunisia without a visa?
faq.answer: The Foreign Ministry's visa table states no length of stay. The Government of Canada says to stay more than 90 days you should contact a Tunisian embassy or consulate before you leave. If you overstay without a valid reason you will be fined; the UK Foreign Office says you can pay on departure at the airport or in advance at some police stations.

faq.question: Can I bring Tunisian dinars in or out of the country?
faq.answer: No. The Government of Canada says importing and exporting Tunisian dinars is prohibited, and the UK FCDO says you are not allowed to take dinars out of Tunisia and advises keeping official exchange receipts. Foreign currency worth TND 20,000 or more must be declared to Customs.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Tunisia?
faq.answer: Tunisia's Foreign Ministry visa-regime table does not list Israel, and says the visa requirement applies to every country not on the list. No official source we could read states whether Israeli passport holders are admitted.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket to enter Tunisia?
